Kathākośa
Jain. Skt. with Pkt. gāthās. containing 27 tales illustrating the usual fruits of different actions of men; beg. with Dhanada an. ending with Nala; 11th Cent. A. D. Bik. 1490. C.. X. C. [Page130-a. 56. IO. 7681. 7682 (with additional stories of Bāhubali, Nala an. Davadantī).

Kathākośa
Jain. Skt. ‘stories of Ārāmatanaya, Hariṣena-Śrīṣeṇa etc.’ BORI. 1266 of 1884-87.
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
Jain. Skt. with a few Pkt. v.. ‘gives stories usually called Samyaktvakaumudīkathā.’ BORI. 1267 of 1884-7.
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
Jain. Skt. prose an. verse; ‘gives stories of Amaracandra etc. ends with a fable possibly from Pañcatantra.’ BORI. 1269 of 1884-87.
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
Jain. Skt. ‘illustrative stories, some of which are Prabandhas about Dinaprabhasūri etc.’ BORI. 582 of 1884-86. Peters. III. p. 404 (no. 582) (inc.).
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
Jain. Skt. prose an. verse. ‘stories about Prasannacandra, Sulasā etc.’ AK. 1324. BORI. 1324 of 1891-5.
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
Jain. Apabhraṁśa. 53 kathās on vratas; first 3 folios have Hariṣeṇa's [Page130-b] Kathākośa. BORI. 478 of 1884-86. Peters. III. p. 400 (no. 478).
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
Jain. Śvet. Skt. prose. ‘possibly contains stories of Samyaktvakaumudī.’ BORI. 583 of 1884-86. Peters. III. p. 404 (no. 583) (inc.).
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
Jain. Skt. with some Pkt. an. Apabhraṁśa verses. ‘stories of Madanarekhā, Sanatkumāra etc.’ AK. 1322. BORI. 1322 of 1891-95.
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
Jain. Skt. prose & verse; gives stories of Devapāla etc.; with some Pkt. AK. 1323. BORI. 1323 of 1891-95.
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākośa
from Karpūraprakara. BORI. 1217 of 1886-92. Peters. IV. p. 45 (no. 1217) (same ms.).
See below Kathāmahodadhi of Somacandra.

Kathākośa
Jain. (collection of moral stories) by Candrakīrti. CPB. 7064-7066.

Kathākośa
Jain. Pkt. by Chatrasena.
See ‘Dig. Jain granthom kī ek Bṛhat Sūcī’ by Pt. Kailasacandra Sastri in Jaina Sid. Bhās. V. iv. p. 226.

Kathākośa
or Kalpamañjarīkathākośa. Jain. by Jayatilakasūri of Āgamagaccha. Jainagranthāvalī p. 267.
See also Kalpamañjarīkathākośa.

Kathākośa
Jain. by Jinakīrti. Dāmanakakathānaka an. Campakaśreṣṭhikathā- [Page131-a. naka from. Text an. transl. ed. by J. Schick, Berlin, 1912.

Kathākośa
Jain. by Devabhadra. See Kathāratnakośa.

Kathākośa
Jain. by Padmanandisūri. Pannalal Bombay 64a. Pannalal Bombay V. B. p. 30.

Kathākośa
Jain. by Brahmadeva.
See Intro. p. 11, Bṛhaddravyasaṅgraha, Rāyacandra Jaina Śāstramālā 5.

Kathākośa
by Merusundara. BORI. 334 of 1871-72.

Kathākośa
or Śakunaratnāvalī. Jain. augury. by Vardhamānasūri (1085 A. D.), pupil of Abhayadeva, the ‘navāṅgīvṛttikṛt’. See Ind. Ant. XXIII. p. 173.
Bik. 713. BORI. 1000 of 1886-92 (Śakunaratnāvalī, probably same).

Kathākośa
also called Bharateśvara Bāhubalivṛtti an. Bharatādikathā. by Śubhaśīlagaṇi, pupil of Munisundara of Tapāgaccha; composed in A. D. 1452. See also A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 41.
BBRAS. 1760-63 (inc.). Bomb. Uni. 2393 (Bharateśvaraº). BORI. 333 of 1871-72. (Adhikāra II). 753 of 1875-76. 413 of 1879-80. 308 of Ā882-83. 620 [Page131-b] of 1884-86. 1306 an. 1307 of 1886-92. (some of these are called Bharateśvaraº). BORI. D. XVII. iii. 888. 889 (inc.). 890-894. Chani 1716. D. p.. 36 (Adhi. II). 117. 148. 330. Gough p. 97 (Adhi. II). Jainagranthāvalī p. 266. JBhP. I. 1958-61. Jhalrapatan p. 135 (with C. in Skt.) (Bharateśvaravṛtti). L. 2710 (Bharatādikathā). Leumann 94. Mandlik Sup. 466 (with C.). Peters. I. p. 128 (no. 308). III. p. 405 (no. 620). IV. p. 49 (nos. 1306 an. 1307). Extr. p. 110.
Pt.. Seth Devchand Lalbhai Jain Pustakoddhar Fund Series 77, 87, Bombay, 1932, 1937, Guj. transl. (2nd edn.), Ahmedabad, 1902.
See also P. E. Pavolini, Eroine brammaniche in un novelliere giainico, Giornale della Soc. Asiatica Italiana, XIII. p.. 89-99, Firenze, 1900.

Kathākośa
Jain. Apabhraṁśa. collection of 53 moral an. religious stories in 53 sandhis; by Śrīcandra Muni, disciple of Vīracandra who belonged to the Kundakunda line; written in 10th or 12th Cent. A. D. for the family of Kṛṣṇa, son of Sajjana of Prāgvāṭa family, a. adviser of King Mūlarāja of Anhilwad.
CPB. 7063. Pannalal Bombay 52. Pannalal Bombay V. B. p. 30.
See Apabhraṁśa sāhitya kā Itihās by Harivamsa Kochar, p.. 348-50, Delhi, 1956; Allahabad University Studies I. p.. 171-72, 1925; Jaina Sid. Bhās. XX. ii. p. 33; Winternitz, HIL. II. p. 543; A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p.. 59-60.

Kathākośa
Jain. by Śrutasāgara. See Vratakathākośa. [Page132-a.

Kathākośa
Jain. by Siṁhanandi. See ‘Dig. Jain granthom ki ek Bṛhat Sūcī’ by Pt. Kailasacandra Sastri in Jaina Sid. Bhās. V. iv. p. 226.

Kathākośa
Jain. by Hariṣeṇa. See Bṛhatkathākośa.

Kathākośa
Jain. Pkt. with some portions in Skt. by Harṣasiṅghagaṇi, written a. Sāraṅgapura; fruits of worshipping gods with gandha, dhūpa etc. BORI. 1268 of 1884-87.
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 42.

Kathākoṣa
or kathAnakakoSa or ka. ko. prakaraNa Jain. Pkt. 30 gāthās an. elaborate C. by Jineśvara, pupil of Vardhamāna; C. 11th Cent. A. D.
Jainagranthāvalī p.. 176. 266 (Vṛtti). Jesalmere Skt. Intro. p. 65 (in a collection); see also p. 17 (no. 150). Praśasti I. p. 88.
See also A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p.. 39-40.
Ed.. Singhi Jain Ser. 11. 1949, with a brief Skt. gloss.

Kathākośa(ṣa)
Jain. identity not known. Alph. List Beng. Govt. p. 22. BORI. 705 of 1875-76. 699 of 1899-1915. BP. p. 167a & b. Chani 1774. D. p. 114 (inc.). Delhi MJP. p. 6 [no. 107]. [no. 108] (with vernacular C.). JBhP. I. 436. 437 (Skt. & Guj.). Leumann 94. Report XLV (inc.). Śravaṇabelgola 113. 161. 388 (d) (in a collection).

Kathākośa_[bālabodha]
Jain. Lakṣmīsena p. 43.

Kathākośa_(ṣa)
or ArAdhanA ka. ko. Jain. by Brahma Nemidatta, disciple of Mallibhūṣaṇa. 16th Cent. A. D. See NCC. II. p. 159b.
The following are add.. mss.--Arrah I. p. 42 (2 mss.). BORI. 1405 an. 1406 of 1886-92. 1044 of 1887-91. Kāśīn. 50. Peters. IV. p. 53 (nos. 1405. 1406). Rep. Raj. & C. I. p. 58. Strassburg Dig. p. 4.
See also A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p.. 62-3.

Kathākośavacanikā
Jain. Śravaṇabelgola 263 (d).

Kathākautuka
kāvya in 15 cantos. by Śrīvara; written in 1451 A. D.; Skt. rendering of Mulla Jāmī's ‘Yusaf-Zulaikhā’ in Persian. Alph. List Beng. Govt. p. 22. BORI. 110 of 1875-76. L. 2585. RASB. VII. 5206. Report VIII.
Pt.. (1) K. M. 72. (2) Ed.. an. German transl. R. Schmidt, Kiel, 1898.

Kathākaumudī

Kathākaumudī

IO. 3300 (Ādi.) 3301 (Sabhā) (name K. kaumudī not mentioned in these two). 3302 (Virāṭa, Bhīṣma an. Mokṣadharma). 3303 (Vana). 3304 (Harivaṁśa) (name K. kau. or a.'s name not found in these two.)

Kathāgrantha
Jain. Jainagranthāvalī p. 266. Pannalal Bombay III. p. 34.

Kathācatuṣṭaya

Kathāchuṭaka

Kathānakakośa

See also A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p. 43. [Page133-a.

Kathānukramaṇikā

Kathāpradīpa

Kathāprabandha

Kathāmahodadhi
Jain. 157 moral an. religious stories based on Karpūraprakara or Sūktāvalī of Hariṣeṇa. by Somacandra, pupil of Ratnaśekhara of Tapāgaccha, composed in 1448 A. D.
BBRAS. 1705. BORI. 775 of 1895-1902. Jainagranthāvalī p. 266. JBhP. I. 440. 453. Peters. III. p.. 316-19 (gives list of the stories). Tod. 48. Weber 2015.
Pt.. along with Karpūraprakara, Jamnagar, 1916.

Kathāmukhatilaka
ny. dealing with the 16 padārthas. by Abhinavagupta.
See NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 300b; also V. Raghavan, JOR. Madras, XIV. p. 328, Works of Abhinavagupta an. Gurunāthaparāmarśa v. 9, Bulletin of the Govt. Ori. Mss. Libr. Madras II. i. 1949. p. 25. [Page133-b]

Kathāmṛtanidhi
or Pañcopākhyānasaṅgraha. a. epitome of Pañcatantra. by Ananta Bhaṭṭa. America 2327. Hall p. 183. IO. 4088.
See Pañcopākhyānasaṅgraha.

Kathāyonā_(?)
Jain. BP. p. 163b.

Kathāratnakośa
Jain. Pkt. Pattan I. p. 334.

Kathāratnakośa
Jain. by Jineśvara. See above Kathākośa.

Kathāratnakośa
or Kathākośa. Jain. in 50 chs. composed a. Broach in 1102 A. D. by Devabhadra, pupil of Sumativācaka an. Prasannacandrasūri.
Jainagranthāvalī p. 266. Peters. III. App. I. p. 134 (no. 288). Praśasti I. p. 49.
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p.. 40-41, where he mentions that the work was under publication by Muni Jinavijaya.

Katharatnasāgara
Jain. in 15 Taraṅgas. by Naracandrasūri, pupil of Devaprabhasūri of Maladhārigaccha.
Jainagranthāvalī p. 266. Pattan I. p. 14.

Kathāratnākara
Jain. BORI. 653 of 1892-95. 777 of 1895-1902 (with Bālāvabodha). BP. p.. 173b. 248a. Chani 153. 2090 (in prose). Pattan I. p. 334. Peters. V. p. 281 (no. 653) (inc.).

Kathāratnākara
or Kathāratnākaroddhāra or Dharmakathāratnākaroº by Uttamaṛṣi. BORI. 1216 of 1886-92. Jainagranthāvalī p. 266. Peters. IV. Extr. p. 80. p. 45 (no. 1216).

Kathāratnākara
Jain. by Hemavijaya, pupil of Kamalavijaya of Tapāgaccha, 1600 A. D.; 258 stories in 10 Taraṅgas; written in Skt. prose an. verse, mixed with Mahārāṣṭrī, Apabhraṁśa etc., nar- [Page134-a. ratives similar to those found in Pañcatantra an. other story books.
BORI. 1270 of 1884-87. 776 of 1895-1902. Dāhilakṣmī XLIII. 8. Jainagranthāvalī p. 57. Jesalmere p. 57. Weber 2016.
Pt.. (1) Jamnagar, 1911. (2) German transl. by J. Hertel, 2 Vol.. Mu7nchen, 1920.

Kathārṇava
Jain. Skt. Fl. J. II. iv. 9.

Kathārṇava
fables. by Śivadāsa.
Bikaner 2783 (ms. d. 1669 A. D.). Fl. 104 (fr.). Oxf. 153a. RASB. VII. 5430. I & II (2 fr..).
See also Weber, Ind. Stud. i. 251 ff. an. Pavolini, Giornale della Soc. Asiatica Italiana IX. 189 ff.

Kathārṇavāṅka
Jain. name of the C. by Padmamandiragaṇi setting forth the illustrative stories, on the Ṛṣimaṇḍalastotra of Dharmaghoṣa (See above p. 45 a-b); composed in 1496 A. D. in the reign of Jinasundarasūri by the grace of Guṇaratnasūri.
BORI. 1210 of 1886-92. 1112 of 1887-91. BORI. D. XIX. i. 68. 69.
See also ibid. notes under no. 61.
Pt.. Ātmavallabhagranthamālā, 1939.

Kathāvatthu
Bud. Pāli. the 5th book of Abhidhamma. cansidered a. the work of Moggaliputta Tissa on the basis of the [Page135-a. original teaching of the Buddha; taken usually a. compiled a. least in part during Aśoka's times.
Br. Mus. Pāli II. p. 110. Cabaton II. 225 (iii). 228 (ºppakaraNa). 243. 257. 422. 423. Colombo p. 49. Colombo D. I. 667. 1792. Fausbo7ll 98. 100. IO. Pāli p. 61 (no. 24c). Kandy II. p. 1. Paris Pāli p. 34 (2 mss.). Providence Pāli no. 14.

See also Rhys Davids, JRAS. 1892, p.. 1-37, on the discussions here; L. de la V. Poussin, JRAS. 1910. p.. 413-23, ‘The five points of Mahādeva an. the Kathāvatthu’, Nalinaksha Dutt, IHQ. XIII. p.. 549-80 on its doctrines.

Kathāvali
or Kahāvali. Jain. Pkt. prose. by Bhadreśvara, earlier than Hemacandra; narrates the lives of 63 Śalākāpuruṣas an. teachers from Kālaka to Haribhadra.
Jainagranthāvalī p. 266. Pattan I. p. 244 (khaṇḍa 2).
See A. N. Upadhye, Bṛhatkathākośa, Intro. p.. 45-46; Kapadia, Canonical Lit. of the Jainas, p. 92. For the Kālakācāryakathā from it, see the [Page135-b] story of Kālaka, the Kālakācāryakathā by W. Norman Brown, Washington, 1933.

Kathāvalī
by Śrutasāgara. Arrah I. p. 42. C.. Vratakathākośa of Śrutasāgara.

CPB. 668.

Lucknow Mus.
